rule_summary: The Family Care Act sets no minimum age. A carer must be suitable for family care by training, experience or personal qualities.
notes: Counties set their own limits. Central Uusimaa and Central Finland ask for at least 25 (rows below); Kymenlaakso's guideline says a carer must be an adult. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county asks people who apply for foster carer preparation to be at least 25.
notes: County practice, not national law.

rule_summary: Central Finland wellbeing services county says a foster carer can be a single person or a couple aged at least 25.
notes: County practice, not national law.

rule_summary: An adoption applicant must be at least 25. A person aged 18 or over can adopt a spouse's child, a child they gave up for adoption, or a child they already have a settled parent-like bond with, or where the child's interests give good reason.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: When adopting a child under 18, the applicant may not be over 50. The adoption can still be confirmed if the applicant was under 50 when the child was named for placement with them.
notes: Suomi.fi states the same limits in plain words. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: The age gap between a child under 18 and the applicant must be at least 18 and at most 45 years. Exceptions are possible, for example for a spouse's child or a settled parent-like bond.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Päijät-Häme wellbeing services county treats an age gap of more than 45 years between the child and the carer as an absolute barrier in ongoing family care. For relatives the age gap is weighed for each child.
notes: County practice. Kymenlaakso's guideline says a child welfare carer should generally be of an age suited to be the child's parent. Read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Central Finland wellbeing services county asks for an age gap of no more than 45 years between the carer and the child. The gap can be larger for short-term family care.
notes: County practice, not national law.

rule_summary: Spouses may adopt a child under 18 only together while married. People who are not married to each other cannot adopt together.
notes: A spouse may adopt alone the other spouse's child, or alone if the other spouse cannot express their will or cannot be found (8 §). Suomi.fi says married same-sex couples can adopt in Finland and from countries that allow it, and that a single applicant must show strong support networks. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Helsinki says many kinds of families can foster: single people, single parents, couples, female and male couples and larger families, as long as the family's situation is stable.
notes: Most county pages read say the same: single people and couples, with or without children.

rule_summary: Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county asks that a couple's relationship has lasted about five years and that they have lived together for about two.
notes: County practice, not national law. It also asks that the family's youngest child is at least 2 years old.

rule_summary: Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county says people living alone and same-sex couples can become foster families, and that having children of your own, or none, is no barrier.
notes: Päijät-Häme lists rainbow families, large families, childless families, blended families and people in flats or houses among its carers.

rule_summary: An applicant who lives in Finland and plans to adopt a child under 18 who lives abroad must use an intercountry adoption service provider licensed by the Adoption Board.
notes: An applicant with a permit under 42 § (adopting without a provider) is exempt. Kela lists Interpedia, Pelastakaa Lapset and the City of Helsinki as providers; Pelastakaa Lapset took no new intercountry clients after 2024. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Helsinki's foster families may live outside Helsinki if they live within 250 km of the city. The children placed are Helsinki residents.
notes: The English page gives the same distance.

rule_summary: Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county lists acute, repeated or long-term income support, or a weak financial position, as a reason a person cannot become a foster carer.
notes: It asks whether a carer could stay at home to care for the child without unreasonable money worries. Päijät-Häme also says regular income support rules out fostering.

rule_summary: Helsinki says a foster carer can work outside the home, but expects one parent to stay at home for a while when the child arrives.
notes: Helsinki pays a higher care fee to a carer at home and an earnings-loss compensation of EUR 1,330 a month for up to one year and one child.

rule_summary: A family care agreement does not create an employment relationship with the wellbeing services county.
notes: As amended by 606/2022, in force from 2023 when the counties took over. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county asks for a doctor's T-certificate (a medical statement) before a person starts as a foster carer.
notes: Central Uusimaa, Central Finland, North Savo and Päijät-Häme also ask for a doctor's statement.

rule_summary: The county must arrange wellbeing and health checks for family carers where needed. A full-time carer must be offered one at least every other year.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: A family home must suit the care given there in health and other conditions, and in its structure, space and equipment. Everyone in the home must accept the person placed, who should have equal standing with the rest of the family.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county asks for a home with enough room: the child must have a room or space of their own with a window by school age at the latest.
notes: County practice, not national law.

rule_summary: Päijät-Häme says a small child in long-term care may not need a room of their own at first, but one must be possible as the child grows. Short-term emergency families must have a room for the child.
notes: County practice. Read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: A family home may care for at most four people at once. This counts the carer's own children under school age and anyone else in the household who needs special care.
notes: As amended by 510/2016. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: A family home may care for up to six people if at least two carers live there and one has suitable training and enough experience of care or upbringing.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: A licensed professional family home may care for up to seven people if at least two carers live there and one has suitable training and experience. Own children under school age count.
notes: Siblings or members of one family may be placed above the limits, and the limits can be varied for another special reason (9 §). Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Before an agreement to care for a child under 18, the authority must ask the would-be carer to show a criminal record extract for work with children.
legal_citation: Laki lasten kanssa työskentelevien rikostaustan selvittämisestä 504/2002, 2 § 2 mom 3 kohta and 5 §
notes: Section 5 still refers to the repealed Family Carers Act 312/1992; Finlex notes the 2015 Act applies instead. Consolidated text current to 9 June 2026; read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county checks a criminal record extract no more than six months old from everyone who becomes a family carer, and checks it again every three years.
notes: Family care guideline in force from 1 February 2026.

rule_summary: In Åland, everyone aged 18 or over in the household must show a valid criminal record extract no more than six months old. KST also checks social, criminal and police records.
notes: Page in Swedish.

rule_summary: When a child is about to be placed, Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county checks the family's child welfare, family and adult social work and family law records in their home county, plus income support data from Kela, population data and police records.
notes: The page cites the Act on the Status and Rights of Social Welfare Clients, 16 §. Most counties read treat current child welfare client status in the applicant's own family as a barrier.

rule_summary: In PRIDE the family and the trainers assess together whether the family is ready to foster. The family gets a written assessment and a certificate, and both partners of a couple must take part.
notes: North Savo. Other counties describe the same joint assessment at the end of preparation. Carers also give criminal record extracts, a doctor's statement and consent to a report from their local social services.

rule_summary: Central Uusimaa makes a shorter family study for families prepared elsewhere or who have fostered for another body: two or three meetings with the parents, plus a request for the earlier body's views.
notes: County practice.

rule_summary: Adoption counselling must help applicants assess their readiness and prepare to be adoptive parents, and must establish whether the conditions for adoption are met. Only wellbeing services counties and licensed adoption agencies may give it, through a social worker who knows adoption.
notes: 21 § and 22 § as amended by 535/2025: the licence now comes from the Licensing and Supervisory Agency. Pelastakaa Lapset says it is the only private provider with this licence. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Adoption counselling ends with a written home study (kotiselvitys) that recommends the applicants or not. Applicants can read and comment on it before it goes further.
notes: Interpedia says counselling covers age, family situation, health, finances, parenting skills, motives and family history.

rule_summary: The Adoption Board may grant an adoption permit if the legal conditions are met and the applicant has had adoption counselling. For a child from abroad, the applicant must also have an intercountry adoption service.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Before the family care agreement is made, a would-be carer must complete the preparation the task needs (ennakkovalmennus).
notes: Every county page read uses PRIDE for child welfare family care. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: PRIDE preparation lasts about six months. It has group meetings, family meetings and personal tasks, led by a foster or adoptive parent and a social worker together.
notes: Pesäpuu ry develops PRIDE in Finland and lists nine group themes. County versions vary: Varha describes about four months with nine three-hour group meetings, and Åland eight sessions.

rule_summary: Southwest Finland's PRIDE has an intake interview, nine three-hour group meetings, at least two family meetings and a final assessment, over about four months.
notes: County practice.

rule_summary: The wellbeing services county is responsible for preparation before approval, and for coaching, work supervision and training during family care, as set in the agreement.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: A responsible worker must be named for each person in family care, and the carer must have enough chances to get support and meet that worker.
notes: County pages list peer groups, work supervision, mentoring and further training. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Family care is arranged under an agreement between the county and the carer (toimeksiantosopimus), or under an agreement with a private family care provider. Professional family care needs a permit and takes place in a professional family home.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Substitute care for a child can be family care, institutional care or another form. Institutional care is used only if family care, with enough support, cannot meet the child's interests.
notes: The choice of placement must also weigh siblings, other close relationships and, where possible, the child's language, culture and religion (50 §). Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 16 June 2026; read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: North Karelia describes short-term family care of up to three months and long-term family care that can last into adulthood.
notes: Ostrobothnia describes short-term placements from a few days to about three months. Most counties also recruit emergency or reception families and substitute carers for carers' days off.

rule_summary: An adoption permit lasts for a set time of no more than two years. The Adoption Board can extend it by up to two years at a time.
notes: If a child is placed within the permit period, it stays valid until the adoption is confirmed. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: The family care agreement must be reviewed when the length or content of care changes, and whenever else there is reason.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Central Uusimaa says a social worker gets in touch within a month of an application to become a foster family.
notes: The only stated response time we found on the county pages read.

rule_summary: Interpedia says adoption counselling takes about a year on average.
notes: Åland's KST says about 10 to 12 months. Interpedia says waiting for a child abroad usually takes a few years.

rule_summary: Before a child is placed outside the home, the county must find out whether the other parent, relatives or other people close to the child could take the child in or support them.
notes: It can be skipped if it is urgent or there is another good reason. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 16 June 2026; read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: When a child lives with a non-parent under a custody order instead of a placement, after the search of the child's network, that carer must be paid the care fee, expenses and start-up compensation.
notes: Added by 510/2016. Child Welfare Act 32 § 3 mom refers to this. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: For special reasons, the preparation can be completed within a year after the placement starts.
notes: Central Finland mentions this in its section on relatives and close people who become carers. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Unless the agreement says otherwise, the carer has a right to a care fee of at least EUR 775 a month for each person in care. The amount is reviewed each year with the wage coefficient of the Employees Pensions Act.
notes: The law gives the base amount; the 2026 indexed minimum is in the next row. No care fee is paid for the carer's own child under 18. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: From 1 January 2026 the minimum care fee is EUR 966.35 a month for each person in care, following Ministry of Social Affairs and Health guidance.
notes: Read in South Ostrobothnia's 2026 fee sheet, which quotes the ministry. Fees above the minimum rise by 2.33% in 2026. Search results show other counties quoting the same figure.

rule_summary: From 1 January 2026 the minimum expense payment (kulukorvaus) is EUR 501.10 a month for each person in care. It covers food, housing, hobbies, personal needs and ordinary health costs.
notes: The law's base amount is EUR 410.66, indexed to the cost-of-living index; payments fell by 0.21% in 2026. Therapy, health and study costs from the child's own needs are paid on top.

rule_summary: Start-up compensation (käynnistämiskorvaus) for necessary costs of starting care is at most EUR 3,558.60 for each person in care in 2026.
notes: The law's base amount is EUR 2,916.43, indexed yearly. Counties often pay less by default: Western Uusimaa pays EUR 1,532.06 and Helsinki EUR 1,411.52, with more on request.

rule_summary: Helsinki pays a care fee of EUR 1,637.23 a month for a child aged 0 to 11 when the carer is at home, and EUR 1,927.16 for a child aged 12 to 17.
notes: A carer in paid work gets EUR 944.36 a month per child. Expenses are paid on top, from EUR 636.48 a month for a child under 7 up to EUR 938.66 for ages 17 to 22. Special care supplements run from EUR 158.98 to EUR 944.36 a month.

rule_summary: Western Uusimaa pays a full-time carer EUR 1,737.86 a month for a child aged 0 to 11 and EUR 2,016.33 for ages 12 to 17 from 1 January 2026.
notes: A full-time carer may also work up to about 40 hours a month. A part-time carer gets EUR 986.75. Expenses range from EUR 705.66 a month (ages 0 to 6) to EUR 1,055.78 (age 17).

rule_summary: North Ostrobothnia pays a basic care fee of EUR 1,538.37 a month in 2026, with two higher bands for more demanding care.
notes: Expenses are EUR 634.49 a month for ages 0 to 12 and EUR 740.25 for ages 13 to 17. Fee sheet dated 9 December 2025.

rule_summary: South Ostrobothnia pays a basic care fee of EUR 1,893.38 a month in 2026, in four bands up to EUR 2,782.31.
notes: The standard expense payment is EUR 830.54 a month.

rule_summary: Kela pays a tax-free adoption allowance for an intercountry adoption: EUR 9,000 for Taiwan, EUR 5,000 for Thailand and EUR 7,000 for other countries, once per child.
notes: The applicant must live permanently in Finland and have the Adoption Board's permit. For more than one child adopted at once, each extra child gets 30% of the full amount. There is no allowance for adopting a child from Finland. People in Åland apply to their municipality.

rule_summary: Adoption counselling is free for applicants.
notes: North Savo, Interpedia and Pelastakaa Lapset say the same. Åland's KST pays for counselling, but families pay their own travel.

rule_summary: An intercountry adoption service provider may charge a fee and its costs, but not more than the real cost of providing the service. It must give a written cost estimate on request.
notes: Interpedia's 2026 costs page lists a registration fee of EUR 550, a yearly fee of EUR 550 and service fees of EUR 1,800, EUR 2,100 and EUR 2,100 at three stages. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Päijät-Häme's PRIDE preparation is free, but it charges EUR 55 for the written materials. The fee is refunded when a long-term placement starts.
notes: The other county pages read say preparation is free. Read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Unless agreed otherwise, a carer has a right to two days off for each calendar month in which they cared for at least 14 days. The county must help arrange care for that time.
notes: Counties recruit substitute carers (sijaishoitajat) to cover these days. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: Unless agreed otherwise, either side can end the agreement with two months' notice. If long-term care ends unexpectedly for reasons outside the carer's control, the carer gets an extra month's care fee.
notes: The extra month was added by 1393/2025, in force from 1 January 2026. It is not paid if a new person can be placed in the notice period. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: A family carer's pension is covered by the Public Sector Pensions Act, and the county must insure the carer against accidents at work and occupational disease.
notes: Kainuu's brochure says the care fee is taxable and builds pension, and the expense payment can be deducted in tax. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 22 December 2025; read in a headless browser because the page is drawn by script.

rule_summary: The county must arrange aftercare when substitute care ends. The duty ends five years after the young person was last a child welfare client, and at 23 at the latest.
notes: As amended by 1283/2023, in force from 1 January 2024, with transitional rules for young people already in aftercare. Åland's KST page still says aftercare can last up to 25. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 16 June 2026; read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: Åland's KST says Åland still applies the Family Carers Act of 1992, not the Family Care Act of 2015. Carers get a monthly fee, expenses and at least two days off a month.
notes: Page in Swedish. The Adoption Act applies in Åland with its municipalities in place of wellbeing services counties (Adoption Act 97 a §).

rule_summary: A child aged 12 or over must consent to the adoption. A younger child cannot be adopted against their will if they are mature enough for it to count.
notes: Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.

rule_summary: The Adoption Board sits in the Licensing and Supervisory Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto). It is the expert, permit and supervisory authority for adoption and the central authority under the Hague Convention.
notes: Amended by 535/2025; before 2026 the Board was part of Valvira. Some county pages still name Valvira. The Board's own site refused our reader. Consolidated text on Finlex, current to 27 June 2025 (amending act 535/2025); read in a headless browser.
